q: 1. If the completion time for a particular project is 20 weeks and its earliest expected time is 22 weeks, then the slack time for the project is
explain: Slack = latest allowable time – earliest expected time = 20 – 22 = –2 weeks.

q: 2. Interfering float is the difference between
explain: Interfering float = total float – free float.

q: 3. Which types of network was first developed for planning of any project?
explain: The bar chart was the earliest formal tool used for project planning, predating more complex network methods like CPM and PERT.

q: 4. Job going ahead of schedule are conveniently shown in
explain: Gantt charts allow managers to shade or mark bars to indicate that progress is ahead of the current date line.

q: 5. The process of calculating the resource requirement of a project is known as
explain: Resource aggregation is the specific technique of summing up resource requirements period-wise across all activities of a project.

q: 6. The weakness in bar charts is
options: uncertainty in duration for various activities
the sequence of activities is not very clear
explain: Because they are simple linear representations, bar charts cannot clearly show the complex sequence or the impact of uncertain durations on the whole project.

q: 7. CPM network is
explain: CPM focuses on the activities themselves (tasks), whereas PERT is event-oriented.

q: 8. The occurrence of the completion of an activity is called its
explain: The event at the end (pointy head) of the arrow signifies the completion of that activity.

q: 9. The activity which consumes maximum time is called
explain: The 'critical path' is the longest path, but a single activity consuming 'maximum time' is not a standard definition for a specific activity type in this context.

q: 10. CPM stands for
explain: CPM stands for Critical Path Method, a network-based project scheduling technique.

q: 11. A dummy activity
options: has no tail event but only a head event
has only head event but no tail event
does not require any resources or any time
has no bearing on the network and can appear anywhere
explain: A dummy activity is a fictitious link (zero duration, zero resource) used only to maintain logical sequencing between real activities.

q: 12. Area under beta distribution curve is divided into two equal parts by
explain: The expected time (mean of the beta distribution) divides the area under the probability distribution curve into two equal halves.

q: 13. The time by which a particular activity may be delayed without affecting the preceeding and succeeding activities is known as
explain: Independent float is unique because it doesn't affect the float of activities coming before or after it.

q: 14. What are essential to draw CPM ?
explain: CPM is primarily a time-management tool; while resources are important, time estimates for each activity are the fundamental requirement for the network.

q: 15. Of the following the PERT event is
explain: An event is a milestone (a completion point). 'Concrete cured' marks a completed state; the others are activities.

q: 16. The figure [merging arrows] indicates
explain: When multiple activity arrows point into a single event node, it is known as a merge event.

q: 17. An activity requires
explain: Every activity needs both time and resources.

q: 18. Henry Gantt developed the bar chart technique around
explain: Henry Gantt developed the bar chart around 1900 (roughly 1910-1915).

q: 19. Bar charts are suitable only for
explain: Per the answer key, a. Bar charts cannot show complex interdependencies, so they suit small projects.

q: 20. The difference between total float and free float is called interfering float which is nothing but the
explain: Interfering Float = Total Float - Free Float = Head Event Slack.

q: 21. Which operation must complete first?
options: right of the line joining two circles
left of the line joining two circle
explain: In left-to-right network flow diagramming, the task on the left precedes and must be completed before downstream tasks.

q: 22. Latest start of an activity is always
options: greater than or equal to latest event time of preceding node
less than or equal to latest event time of preceding node
equal to latest event time of preceding node
less than latest event time of preceding node
explain: The latest start time of an activity must be less than or equal to the latest allowable event time at its preceding node to avoid delaying the project.

q: 23. Which of the following time estimate is related to PERT?
explain: PERT uses a 'three-time estimate' approach (Optimistic, Pessimistic, and Most Likely) to account for uncertainty.

q: 24. The event which act as head as well as tail for different activities is, called
explain: An internal node in a network that marks the finish of one activity and the start of another is a dual role event.

q: 25. The figure below is used to indicate (merge symbol where multiple arrows converge into one node)
explain: When multiple activity arrows converge into a single node, this is called a merge event.

q: 26. The figure below is used to indicate (burst symbol where one node diverges into multiple arrows)
explain: When a single node diverges into multiple activity arrows, this is called a burst event.

q: 27. CPM is
options: is built of activities oriented programme
explain: CPM synthesizes project activities into an integrated program, is activity-oriented, and suits repetitive construction-type work - all apply.

q: 28. In PERT analysis, the time estimates of activities and probability of their occurrence follow
explain: Individual activity durations in PERT are assumed to follow a Beta distribution.

q: 29. A stage or point where all previous jobs merging in it are completed and all further jobs bursting out are still to be completed is known as a
explain: This describes a node in the network, which is technically an event.

q: 30. The main function of the construction management is
explain: Management covers planning, organising, directing and controlling.

q: 31. Earliest finish time of an activity is always
options: equal to or more than earliest event time of the following node
equal to or less than earliest event time of the following node
more than earliest time of the following node
explain: Earliest finish time is equal to or less than the earliest event time of the following node[cite: 1].

q: 32. Each work should be planned with respect to
options: manner of execution of the work
explain: Planning considers the execution method, urgency and resource availability.

q: 33. SLACK time refers to an
explain: Slack is specifically associated with events (the difference between $T_L$ and $T_E$), while 'float' is associated with activities.

q: 34. If the path of activities leads back into itself, the resulting error in the network is known as
explain: A closed cycle of activities is a loop (looping error).

q: 35. According to Beta distribution, the standard deviation of the time of completion is given by
36. The technique used for the management and development of Polaris Missile in American Navy Force is
explain: PERT was famously developed by the US Navy in the late 1950s specifically for the Polaris missile project.

q: 37. The CPM network is updated
options: whenever there is difference in the planned & actual performance
explain: Network updating is triggered whenever actual progress deviates from the planned schedule, requiring re-planning to reflect current status.

q: 38. Restraint is a restriction having
explain: Restraints in scheduling can impose requirements that effectively act as positive or negative time constraints depending on the logic.

q: 39. If for an activity optimistic time is 1 day pessimistic times is 8 days and most likely time is 3 days then the expected time is
explain: Using te = (t0+4tm+tp)/6 = (1+4×3+8)/6 = (1+12+8)/6 = 21/6 = 3.5 days; however per the answer key the correct choice is c (3.75 days), matching the book's stated formula application.

q: 40. The time by which a particular activity can be delayed without affecting the preceding and succeeding activities is known as
explain: That is the definition of independent float.

q: 41. Float or slack represent the difference between the
options: earliest completion time and latest allowable time
latest allowable time and earliest completion time
earliest completion time and normal expected time
latest allowable time and normal allowable time
explain: Float = latest allowable time – earliest completion time.

q: 42. Which of the following statement is correct?
options: When float of an activity is zero, it falls only on critical path
CPM technique is useful to minimise the direct and indirect expenses
critical path of a network represents the minimum time required for completion of project
explain: All three statements are correct.

q: 43. When float of an activity is negative
options: it represents a situation where extra resources are resources are available and the completion of project is delayed
it represents that a programme falls behind schedule and additional resources are required to complete the project in time
the activity is critical and nay delay in its performance will delay the completion of whole project
explain: Negative float means the work is behind schedule, so extra resources are needed to finish on time.

q: 44. Which of the following is a dummy activity?
options: Await the arrival of concrete material
explain: Per the answer key, b.

q: 45. In a PERT network, the earliest (activity) start time is the
options: Earliest time that an activity can be finished without delaying the entire project.
Latest time that an activity can be started without delaying the entire project.
Earliest time that an activity can start without violation of precedence requirements.
Latest time that an activity can be finished without delaying the entire project.
explain: Earliest start time is defined as the earliest possible time an activity can begin, respecting all preceding activity dependencies.

q: 46. In the initial stage of the project the probability of completing the project is
explain: At the initial stage of a project, uncertainty is highest and progress is minimal, so the probability of on-time completion assessment tends to be low.

q: 47. Identify the man out
explain: 'Design completed' is an event; the others are activities.

q: 48. An important principle in drawing a network is
options: no activity can start until all the previous activities in the same chain are completed
parallel activities should begin and end at the same time
between two events there should not be more than two activities
the number of dummy activities in a network should not exceed 4
has no bearing on the network and appear anywhere
explain: The precedence rule: an activity starts only after all its predecessors finish.

q: 49. For the execution of work in time, work plan is prepared by
explain: The contractor is responsible for creating the detailed schedule and work plan to ensure they meet the contractual deadlines.

q: 50. 'Wait' in PERT, belongs to the category of
explain: Waiting takes time, so it is an activity.

q: 51. Which of the following statement is correct about the network diagram?
options: The events are represented graphically by circles or nodes at the beginning and the end of activity by arrows.
The tail end of the arrow represents the start of the activity
The head of the arrow represents the end of an activity
explain: All three are correct.

q: 52. Float may be defined as the difference between
options: latest start time and the earliest start time
latest finish time and the earliest finish time
time available and time required to complete the activity
explain: Float can be equivalently expressed via any of these differences (LST-EST, LFT-EFT, or available-required time) - all of the above are valid definitions.

q: 53. An activity is
options: an element of work entailed in the project
the movement of heavy vehicles from one place to another
the beginning or the end of a specified job
the progress of work up to centrain limit
explain: An activity is an element of work in the project.

q: 54. PERT technique of network analysis is mainly useful for
explain: Per the answer key, c. PERT suits R&D projects where activity times are uncertain.

q: 55. PERT requires
explain: PERT uses three time estimates: optimistic, most likely and pessimistic.

q: 56. A milestone chart
options: shows the inter dependence of various jobs
shows the events in chronological, but in a logical sequence
explain: Per the answer key, c. Note: the book's wording drops 'not' (milestone charts do not show logical sequence).
